# Documentation Index

Index for discovering relevant documents during Plan and Explore execution

## Usage

Identify and read task-related sections below:

- Modify `cmd/` or CLI behavior → Read **Specifications** section (CLI, Requirements)
- Modify YAML configuration handling → Read **Specifications** section (Configuration, Requirements)
- Make design decisions or evaluate scope → Read **Project Overview** section
- Edit documents under `docs/` → Read **Contributing** section
- Modify the release workflow, `.goreleaser.yaml`, or `Dockerfile` → Read **Contributing** section (Release Workflow)
- Change explanations for users → Read **User Guide** section and **Contributing** section (Documentation Policy)

## Specifications

- [Requirements](docs/spec/requirements.md): Functional requirements, quality requirements, and invariants of reco - Use when implementing or changing features, or checking supported scope and safety guarantees
- [CLI](docs/spec/cli.md): Commands (`plan`, `apply`, `show`), options, credential selection, interactive approval, output, and exit codes - Use when modifying `cmd/`, adding commands or options, or changing user-visible output and exit codes
- [Configuration](docs/spec/configuration.md): YAML configuration structure, types, allowed values, combinations, management scope interpretation, and input validation - Use when modifying configuration parsing or validation, or adding supported repository settings

## Design

- [Domain Model](docs/design/domain.md): Core concepts of reco and the distinctions between them (declaration, selection, and repository identity; management units vs. managed settings; setting values shared across contexts; side effects; current state vs. observation result and the points in time of observation; reconciliation vs. applicability; change plan structure; logical change vs. update operation; approval and change preconditions; the contexts each concept belongs to) - Use when naming domain types, deciding what a concept means, or checking that code keeps these distinctions
- [Architecture](docs/design/architecture.md): Logical components and their boundaries, change planning and execution control, pre-validation, approval and per-update precondition checks, GitHub API trust boundary (redirects, unmanaged-setting preservation, non-atomic updates), and result classification - Use when placing responsibilities across packages, implementing the plan/apply flow, or changing how GitHub updates are issued and verified

## Research

- [Research](docs/research/README.md): Purpose of the GitHub API research documents, how they are split, and the conventions they follow (grounded only in GitHub official docs, API version basis, developer-verified behavior as notes) - Use when adding a GitHub API fact or a new endpoint document
- [GitHub OpenAPI Excerpt](docs/research/openapi.json): Excerpt of GitHub's official OpenAPI 3.0 description limited to the operations reco uses and the components they reference, generated by `scripts/openapi/update.sh` - Use when checking request or response field types and enum values of an endpoint reco uses
- [GitHub REST API Common](docs/research/rest-api.md): GitHub REST API contract shared by every endpoint reco uses (request URL and headers, API versions, redirects, failure responses, rate limits, conditional requests, token types, scopes, and repository roles) - Use when a spec or design needs a GitHub fact that is not specific to one endpoint
- [GitHub Repositories API](docs/research/repositories.md): Repository get and update endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, merge-related field visibility, repository name vs. ID and rename redirects, general setting fields and update behavior, and the settings-screen items they correspond to) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about repository identity or general settings
- [GitHub Actions Permissions API](docs/research/actions-permissions.md): Actions permissions, selected actions, workflow permissions, and access from workflows outside the repository endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, fields, update units, observed side effects, and the settings-screen items they correspond to) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about GitHub Actions permission settings

## User Guide

- [User Guide](docs/user-guide/README.md): Entry point of the user guide for reco users, not implementers (intended readers and the documents to read for each user goal, split into main documents and optional detail documents) - Use when choosing which user-facing document to read or adding a new one
- [Overview](docs/user-guide/overview.md): What reco solves and whether it fits the reader, for users evaluating adoption (the problem it addresses, the declare / `plan` / `apply` flow and `show`, the settings it manages described by what they control and mapped to GitHub settings-screen items, and the safety promises users care about before first use, plus the caveat that a stopped `apply` is not rolled back) - Use when explaining what reco is and whether it suits a user's needs, or when changing supported settings, scope, or safety promises that this summary repeats
- [Configuration Guide](docs/user-guide/configuration.md): How to write the configuration file for users (file location and structure, tables of keys, allowed values, and meanings for `general`, `actions.permissions`, `actions.workflow`, and `actions.access` with the points to watch when writing them, unwritten settings staying unmanaged, listing multiple repositories, common mistakes) - Use when explaining to users how to declare settings, or when changing configuration behavior that users rely on
- [Actions Policy Switching](docs/user-guide/actions-policy.md): Optional detail document for users on switching `allowed_actions` between `selected` and other values (GitHub discarding `selected_actions` and the `Side effect:` line, restoring discarded values, the two updates and the temporary state between them) - Use when explaining what happens on GitHub when the Actions permission policy changes, or when changing that behavior
- [Safety Guide](docs/user-guide/safety.md): Optional detail document on how reco keeps changes safe, in plain user-facing terms (not changing unwritten settings, reading every repository before updating, changing only what was approved, stopping when settings change after approval or a problem occurs, confirming the result before reporting completion, keeping the token out of output, and what reco does not do such as rollback, retry, or following redirects) - Use when explaining reco's safety behavior to users, or when changing an invariant or behavior that users rely on for trust
- [Command Reference](docs/user-guide/commands.md): Commands, options, and their defaults for users (`show`, `plan`, `apply`; `--repo` takes one repository, which for `plan` / `apply` must be declared in the configuration file; example output of each command and how to read the plan lines (including `Applicability: not applicable` and `Plan cannot be applied.`) and the `apply` result words; what `apply` does and when it asks for approval, which only `y` or `yes` on a terminal grants; `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` selection; stdout vs. stderr and the one-line JSON error; exit code `0` on success and `1` on failure, including `plan` with a change that cannot be applied) - Use when explaining commands, options, approval, or exit codes to users, or when changing CLI behavior that users script against
- [Installation](docs/user-guide/installation.md): Installing and running reco for users (GitHub Releases archives installed with copy-paste curl commands per OS and architecture, a first `show` with `GH_TOKEN`, and pulling the GHCR image by a version tag and running `plan` in a mounted working directory) - Use when explaining how to install or run reco, or when changing distribution or image behavior that users rely on
- [Authentication](docs/user-guide/authentication.md): Preparing the token for users (passing `gh auth token` output in `GH_TOKEN`, what `gh auth login` / `gh auth token` do, token permissions not exceeding the owner's role, passing a token of an account with the Admin role, and roles below Write failing) - Use when explaining which token and role reco needs, or when changing credential behavior that users rely on
- [Verification](docs/user-guide/verification.md): Optional verification of downloads for advanced users (`gh attestation verify` for archives and the container image via `container-image.txt`, why `SHA256SUMS` alone is not enough, running the verified image by digest) - Use when explaining how to verify release artifacts, or when changing the release workflow's attestation
- [Getting Started](docs/user-guide/getting-started.md): Tutorial that walks a user through one setting on one repository (`show`, writing `reco.yaml` with `general.delete_branch_on_merge`, `plan`, approving `apply`, confirming `No changes.`, and reverting by declaring the old value) - Use when explaining the first use of reco, or when changing output or behavior that the first run shows
- [Operations](docs/user-guide/operations.md): Procedures for managing multiple repositories (adding a repository after checking it with `show` and applying only it with `--repo`, narrowing a run to one repository, ordering repositories since updates follow the file order and stop at the first incomplete repository, periodic `plan` to notice drift, reverting values, and stopping management by removing lines or repositories) - Use when explaining day-to-day use of reco across repositories, or when changing selection, ordering, or stop behavior that these procedures rely on
- [Troubleshooting](docs/user-guide/troubleshooting.md): What to do after an error or an unexpected `apply` result, organized by symptom (reading the one-line JSON error; a missing configuration file, configuration mistakes, an undeclared `--repo`, a missing or invalid token, insufficient role (`403` / `404` / missing fields), `Plan cannot be applied.` with how to read the reason and fix the declaration, approval not available or declined, an `apply` that stopped partway with the meaning of `Update request` and `Desired state`, auto-merge not applied on GitHub Free private repositories, and a table of rarer errors and lines such as rate limits, `redirect not followed`, `Precondition:`, and `Other settings:`) - Use when explaining to users how to recover from errors or partial results, or when changing error messages or result lines that users act on

## Project Overview

- [Constitution](docs/CONSTITUTION.md): Purpose, problem statement, value proposition, design principles, and non-goals of reco - Use when making design decisions, resolving tradeoffs between principles, or judging whether a feature is in scope

## Contributing

- [Documentation Policy](docs/contributing/docs-policy.md): Responsibilities and sources of truth of each document, identifiers (`FR`, `QR`, `INV`), Relationships (`alignment`, `grounding`, `checks`), consistency checks on change, the split of readers (implementers for most of `docs/`, reco users for `docs/user-guide/`), and the rules for the user guide (readers, relation to the specifications, writing rules on caveats, terms, links, and duplication, main vs. detail documents, checks when changing documents, output examples) - Use when adding or changing requirements, identifiers, or Relationship tables, when editing specs and designs, or when editing the user guide
- [Release Workflow](docs/contributing/release.md): Tag-triggered release to GitHub Releases and GHCR (job order and permissions, artifacts, build settings, container image, provenance attestation, partial publication and re-runs, user-side verification, pinning of actions and tools) - Use when modifying `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.goreleaser.yaml`, or `Dockerfile`, or when cutting a release
